terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

structureKind: single articulated character bust, no limbs in frame
motionPotential: static display prop with subtle idle motion (head micro-turn / breathing) -- no locomotion, no full rig
objectClass.notes: Adult male head+neck+upper-torso bust, cropped at mid-torso (no arms/hips/legs). Built as a stylized LOW-POLY / FACETED character, not realistic or photoreal -- geometry is deliberately faceted (flat-shaded triangle/quad planes visible as a feature, not smoothed away) and every material's albedo is drawn from the site's own acetate-plane palette (indigo/sienna/amber/ink) rather than the photo's literal colors, per explicit user direction: this model IS the hero portrait's flat acetate planes given a third dimension.

reasoning: Silhouette is moderately complex: an irregular, asymmetric curl-cluster hair mass is the single hardest shape to read (silhouetteComplexity 6), everything else (face-plate, torso) is a simpler organic primitive.

3 macro parts (head, neck, torso/hoodie) each with several meso sub-assemblies (hair mass, face-plate, ears; hood, zipper track, torso panel, henley collar) -- moderate hierarchy depth (3), not shallow.
repetitionDensity is low (3): the hair clump system (5-15 major masses per reconstruction.md) is the only real repetition system on this subject -- no fastener rows, no tiled trim.

materialLayerCount is real (6 distinct surfaces: skin, hair, hoodie fleece, henley knit, metal, cord) even though every one gets a flat, low-roughness faceted treatment rather than full PBR detail -- material COUNT drives spec depth, not per-material complexity.

occlusionRisk is real (4): back/sides of head, right ear, torso back are all unobserved from this single frontal photo -- flagged in unknownsToResolveBeforeImplementation, handled by reasonable low-poly simplification rather than invented specificity.

actionReadinessNeed is 1 (near-zero): this ships as a static interactive prop (orbit-drag + a small hand-coded idle motion), explicitly NOT the animated-character profile -- no skeleton, no walk/idle animation contract, per user's own scoping.

Net tier: complex is right for the hierarchy/material-count reasons above, but this is a STYLIZED complex bust, not an ultra-complex realistic one -- the low-poly faceted treatment caps geometric/material fidelity deliberately.

specDepthDecision.rationale: complex tier from real component/material count (see complexity.reasoning), but needsActionReadyHierarchy is intentionally false: this is a static/idle-only prop, not a rigged action-ready character.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

details.description: Voluminous curl-cluster hair mass, fuller/higher on proper-left side of the part, receding slightly at both temples. Warm amber/gold-brown, rim-lit brighter at the crown, darker brown underneath.

Straight moderately-thick eyebrows, medium-set eyes with visible upper-lid crease, straight nose bridge, closed asymmetric smile (proper-right corner raised more), light even stubble across jaw/upper lip.
Visible ear carrying a single hoop/stud earring -- an asymmetric identity mark (right ear has no earring).
Ear almost fully occluded by hair in this view; build mirrored from earLeft's geometry, without the earring.
Neck column, same skin material as the face plate, partially occluded by the henley/hoodie collar at its base.
Hoodie's hood folded down, draped/resting on the shoulders and upper back rather than worn up -- soft-body cloth drape, not a rigid shell.
Vertical metal zipper track (teeth + pull tab), unzipped to mid-chest, flanked by two white cotton drawstrings hanging from the hood, each ending in a small metal cord-lock aglet.
Hoodie fleece body -- deep wine/aubergine, very high roughness (napped, matte), large soft fold/wrinkle cluster at the chest and underarms from fabric slack.
Teal henley collar with 2-3 dark buttons, visible through the hoodie's unzipped V -- a distinct knit material layered beneath the hoodie fleece.
small metal cord-lock aglets terminating each drawstring

proportions.note: Bust crop: only crown-to-mid-torso is in frame (~3.13 HU visible from crown to the image's bottom crop, not a true crown-to-hip torso measurement). legs/hipWidth/torso are genuinely not observable here -- left null rather than guessing a stock adult ratio, per reconstruction.md's own instruction. shoulderWidth (1.95 HU) falls inside the doc's own realistic-build range, which cross-checks the head-unit measurement as sane. torso=1.78 is crown-to-crop-bottom (partial, not crown-to-hip -- there is no hip in frame). legs/hipWidth are 0.0 by convention (not applicable to a bust), not measurements.

pose.type: frontal-neutral bust, near-camera-facing with a very slight head turn (within measurement noise -- treated as neutral)
pose.jointAngleConfidence: neck/shoulders measured (frontal, level) at high confidence; elbow/wrist/hip/knee/ankle are entirely below the crop -- left at neutral rest defaults with confidence 0, not measured, per reconstruction.md's occluded-joint rule. The bust build (see spec) never instantiates arms/legs, so these defaults are inert.

faceLandmarks.note: hairline is well above the doc's typical 0.0-0.15 band -- a real, measured deviation from this subject's voluminous curly hair covering more of the forehead than a typical short-hair reference, not an error. eyeSpacing measured at the tighter end of the stylized 0.2-0.35 range since the target is a recognizable adult likeness, not a cute/chibi read.

definitionOfDone: The rendered model matches the reference silhouette, primary proportions, visible component hierarchy, material response, and most recognizable local features for the selected fidelity tier.

featureGroups.name: Overall silhouette and proportions
qualityCriteria: Bounding shape, dominant curves, negative spaces, and scale relationships are explicitly described.
failureModes: model reads as a generic placeholder instead of the reference object
major proportions are guessed without evidence

featureGroups.name: Primary structure and hierarchy
qualityCriteria: Major parts, joints, seams, contact points, and parent-child relationships are named before code generation.
failureModes: large visible parts are merged into one mesh
component hierarchy is too shallow for the observed complexity

featureGroups.name: Attachment and joint correctness
qualityCriteria: Every visible child appendage, branch, limb, handle, connector, tube, cable, horn, wing, leg, or hinged part has an attachment contract with parent socket, localStart/localEnd, contact type, embed/overlap, and gap tolerance.
failureModes: child part root floats away from the parent
branch/limb/tube is centered in space instead of pivoting from its root
parent-child transform mixes world and local coordinates

featureGroups.name: Surface material response
qualityCriteria: Albedo zones, roughness, normal/bump/displacement intent, cavity dirt, edge wear, and local overrides are specified where visible.
Important materials define independent albedo, roughness, height/normal, and AO responses instead of reusing one texture for unrelated PBR channels.
Surface response is decomposed into macro, meso, and micro frequency bands with scale and amplitude tied to object scale.
failureModes: local material variation is missing or not tied to image evidence

featureGroups.name: Reference color, material, and lighting response
qualityCriteria: Material-pass names the reference-derived albedo palette, roughness variation, tactile normal/bump/displacement response, and local masks.
When a source image is available, run reference PBR extraction and require confidence >= 0.7 before treating maps as implementation-ready.
Lighting-pass names key/fill/rim or environment light, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadow behavior.
Neutral, grazing-angle, and reference-matched renders prove that surface relief survives relighting and is not painted into albedo.
failureModes: model has acceptable shape but reads as flat shaded or plastic
colors are a generic average instead of reference-observed local color zones
lighting is evenly ambient and cannot reproduce the source value range

visualDeltaChecks: local feature placement and scale delta

Do not proceed to code if visible local features are described only in prose and not attached to components/materials/evidenceRefs.
Do not proceed past structural-pass if attached child parts lack attachment.parentSocket, localStart, localEnd, embedDepth/overlap, and gapTolerance.
Do not pass material look-dev when albedo is reused as roughness, height, normal, or AO.

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

specRefineTriggers: local feature not traceable to viewEvidence
codeRefineTriggers: spec is adequate but generated geometry/material does not match
lighting hides geometry or material response
stopCriteria: target fidelity reached or user accepts current approximation
remaining gaps require new reference images or manual art

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

featureReviewTargets.name: Face landmarks incl. recessed eye sockets

referencePbrExtraction.acceptedLimitation: Explicitly skipped: this build uses flat per-material palette colors (materials[].baseColor), never texture-extracted PBR maps, per the committed faceted-low-poly direction. See materials[].notes on every material for the reasoning.

mustAvoid: plastic-looking smooth bark, stone, cloth, foliage, or aged material
local color/detail described only in prose without material masks
claiming exact PBR recovery when confidence is below the target threshold
reference lighting copied without separating material readability

screenshotReview: Compare albedo palette and local color zones.
Compare cavity dirt, edge wear, stains, moss, scratches, or other local masks.
Compare key/fill/rim structure, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadows.
Capture a neutral-light render to verify material readability without reference lighting.
Capture a grazing-light close-up to expose flat normals, uniform roughness, tiling, and plastic highlights.
Capture a reference-matched render from the same camera framing as the source.

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro/meso component should be generated as a stable named Object3D pivot node with a mesh child, action metadata, optional sockets, collider proxy, and destruction metadata.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For attached child parts, put the pivot at the semantic root/socket and build visible geometry from localStart to localEnd.
Represent hinge, socket, detachable, and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies for runtime physics instead of visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups and a small number of procedural fragments over random mesh explosion.

assumptions: Back/sides of the head beyond the visible fringe are not observed (single frontal photo) -- built as a simplified, plausible rounded continuation of the hair mass, explicitly approximate, never claimed as measured.
Right ear geometry is mirrored from the visible left ear (minus the earring), since the source photo occludes it.
True skull/nose profile depth is inferred proportionally from the measured head-unit/shoulder-width ratios, not from a second photo angle.
Iris color defaults to warm dark-brown; the source photo's lighting makes the exact shade uncertain.

Every material's albedo is deliberately drawn from the site's own 4-color acetate-plane palette rather than the photo's literal colors (wine hoodie -> indigo, teal henley -> ink, etc.) -- a committed stylization choice, not a measurement gap.

coordinateFrame.front: +Z (face-forward, camera-facing side in the reference photo)
coordinateFrame.origin: base of the neck (where neck meets the visible torso top) -- a bust has no pelvis/hip, so this replaces the generator's default hip-height root.
coordinateFrame.scaleReference: 1 world unit = 1 measured head-height (anatomy.json headUnit=0.219 of the source image height). All component dimensions/transforms in componentTree are authored directly in this frame -- no post-hoc rescale needed.

silhouette.boundingShape: An ovoid head (with an irregular, asymmetric curl-mass hair volume bulging past the head ellipsoid) atop a short cylindrical neck, atop a wide-shouldered tapered-cone torso cropped at mid-torso -- no arms, hips, or legs in frame.
silhouette.symmetry: bilateral overall (face, torso, shoulders), with two deliberate asymmetries preserved as identity features: hair fuller on proper-left, smile corner higher on proper-right, plus a left-only earring
dominantCurves: irregular hair-mass bulge (the single hardest-to-read silhouette element)
torso taper from shoulder to crop-bottom
negativeSpaces: gap between drawstrings and torso (they hang free, tethered only at the hood)
unzipped hoodie V exposing the henley collar

albedo.samplingNotes: Color drawn from the site's own acetate-plane palette (app/app.css / scripts/generate-hero-planes.mjs), not the photo's literal color -- see objectClass.notes.

textureProjection.texelDensityIntent: no texture -- flat vertex-color/material color only

roughness.localResponse: very slightly lower roughness (subtler sheen) at the nose bridge and forehead facets, matching the source photo's own highlight placement (image-analysis.md Layer 6).

shaderNotes: flatShading:true is load-bearing -- the facets are the entire surface language.

materials.notes: Deliberately flat, no procedural surface texture: this is a faceted low-poly material -- shading variation comes from real-time lighting hitting flat per-face normals (flatShading:true), not from a painted macro/meso/micro noise stack. Matches the hero portrait's own flat acetate-plane treatment. Amber (--accent) reused directly as skin tone -- the lightest, warmest palette color, and the same one the hero portrait's own highlight plane uses for skin.

repetitionSystems.rule: reconstruction.md: prefer 5-15 major stylized clumps over strand geometry for single-image hair reconstruction. 8-10 low-poly clump primitives (irregular ellipsoids/cones), layered front-to-back, matching the observed silhouette (fuller proper-left, receding at both temples) -- not individually identity-critical, but the CLUSTER shape is.

buildPasses.goal: Lock head-unit proportions (anatomy.json) and the overall silhouette: torso taper, neck, head ellipsoid, hair-mass bulge.
acceptance: silhouette reads as a bust, not a full figure
shoulder-width:head-height ratio matches the measured 1.95 HU

buildPasses.goal: Attach every meso/micro part at its measured socket: ears, brows, eyes, nose, mouth on the head; hood/zipper/collar/drawstrings on the torso.
acceptance: no child part floats away from its parent

buildPasses.goal: Facet the hair mass into 8-10 stylized clump primitives (repetitionSystems.hairClumps) and refine the face-plate shapes (asymmetric smile, brow arch) to match the measured faceLandmarks.
acceptance: hair silhouette is asymmetric (fuller proper-left) not a symmetric dome
smile reads as closed and asymmetric, not neutral/mirrored

buildPasses.goal: Apply the six acetate-palette materials (flatShading:true) with the localOverrides now on hoodieFleece/hairMass/skin for the identity-defining marks.
acceptance: every material reads as one of the four site palette hues
earring/stubble/fold-cluster local overrides are visible at their measured regions

buildPasses.goal: Wire the key/fill/rim lights from lightingFromPhoto, ACES filmic tone mapping, and a soft contact shadow beneath the bust.
acceptance: shadow-side facets stay readable (indigo ambient fill), never fully black
amber rim light echoes the hero section's own light-cone

buildPasses.goal: Drag-to-orbit control plus a small hand-coded idle motion (subtle head micro-turn / breathing) -- no skeleton, no walk cycle.
acceptance: orbit drag feels physically damped, matching the site's react-spring motion language
idle motion is subtle enough to read as 'alive', not distracting

buildPasses.goal: Merge static geometry into as few draw calls as practical, verify 60fps on a mid-tier laptop GPU, confirm the model disposes cleanly if the hero later swaps it out.
acceptance: fpsTarget (60) holds during idle motion + orbit drag

reviewHistory.summary: Divine Eye: reject/refine-code (silhouette IoU 0.536, scale delta 0.477, both below hard-gate thresholds; objectness 0.546). This is the tool's honest, unmodified verdict. Per grimoire/review/self_correction.md's own photo-vs-procedural caveat, chasing this score further for a deliberately stylized low-poly bust risks distorting the model rather than improving it. User reviewed the side-by-side comparison and explicitly authorized proceeding to structural-pass despite the score -- see .img2threejs/tier1-exception.md for the full reasoning and sculptPipeline.completedPasses for the manual advance this authorized.
matched: multi-angle holds as a real volume, not a degenerate flat plane (diagnose_render_multi_angle: degenerate=false, min ratio 1.02)
torso taper direction and width now measured from the real photo's alpha silhouette, not guessed
mismatches: silhouette IoU 0.536 vs 0.85 required -- torso/arm bulk still narrower than photo, hair is a smooth dome vs photo's irregular curl silhouette
scale delta 0.477 -- render's overall subject-to-frame proportion doesn't match the photo's crop

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Reach accepted visual fidelity first, then optimize without removing reference-critical geometry or surface layers.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: Front-upper-right key, matching the source photo's soft daylight-from-above read (image-analysis.md Layer 6). Drives the eye catchlight offset per reconstruction.md.
Low-intensity indigo-tinted ambient fill so shadow-side facets never go fully black -- keeps the faceted geometry readable from every rotation angle.

Warm amber rim from upper-back-left, matching the source photo's own backlit-crown highlight on the hair (Layer 6: 'bright warm-blonde rim-lit crown'). Also echoes the hero section's own light-cone color, tying the 3D piece back to the page it sits on.

ACES filmic tone mapping, renderer exposure ~1.0, so the amber rim light doesn't clip to flat white on the faceted highlight facets. A soft contact shadow (ground shadow) is cast beneath the bust onto the hero's own light-cone plane so it reads as sitting in the scene, not pasted over it.

proceduralStrategy: Create stable pivot groups, sockets, collider proxies, and destruction metadata before visual polish.
Refine forms with bevels, tapers, bends, and procedural noise.
Run reference PBR extraction for important source-image materials and stop when confidence is below the target threshold.
Add material variation before adding expensive micro-geometry.
animationAnchors: root pivot node supports whole-object translation, rotation, scale, and visibility changes
component pivot groups support later local transforms without rebuilding geometry
destructionAnchors: actionProfile.destruction.fractureGroup marks detachable or breakable component sets
component seams and sockets define plausible break points instead of random explosions
risks: Faceted low-poly hair is the single highest risk of reading as a generic placeholder rather than this specific person's silhouette -- the clump cluster's overall shape (asymmetric, fuller proper-left) carries more likeness weight than any individual facet.

A bust with no lower body/arms could look like an accidental crop rather than a deliberate framing choice if the torso's cut edge isn't handled cleanly (e.g. a flat cap with a subtle bevel, not a raw open cylinder end).
Recoloring real materials (wine hoodie, teal henley) into the 4-color palette trades photographic fidelity for site cohesion -- an explicit, user-approved trade, not an oversight.
